CheckTitle: Ensure overly permissive identity policies include condition-based access boundaries in ABAC environments
Description: IAM identity policy statements that allow broad permissions (Action: '*' or Action: 'service:*') on all resources (Resource: '*') without any condition block bypass intended ABAC access segmentation. In environments using attribute-based access control, unconstrained wildcard policies are not limited by tag-based conditions.
Risk: Broad allow statements on all resources without conditions violate least-privilege principles and bypass the access segmentation model. In ABAC-oriented environments, these statements leave access unrestricted by any principal tag, resource tag, request tag, or other contextual attribute, negating the ABAC design intent.
Remediation: Narrow Action and Resource scope to the minimum required. Where ABAC is intended, add tag-based conditions (aws:PrincipalTag, aws:ResourceTag, aws:RequestTag, or aws:TagKeys). Review all wildcard policies for unnecessary breadth.
SeverityBasis: AWS IAM ABAC documentation (attribute-based access control design); NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 AC-6 (Least Privilege), AC-3 (Access Enforcement); medium severity reflects that exploitation requires an attacker to first compromise the overly-permissive principal
AuthoritativeSource: AWS IAM ABAC documentation; NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5
CISControl: N/A — ABAC condition enforcement is not individually enumerated in CIS AWS 3.0.0
